# Completeness — where did we stop

Three states, **derived from evidence** rather than declared:

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `sketched` | rungs 0-1 — the node is named, and may say what it is for, but what is inside it is not established |
| `documented` | rungs 2-3, or rung 4 or deeper whose owning document has not certified it as verified — its contents are **enumerable**; it may or may not also be read by a gate or pinned by a probe, and `why` names the rung it stopped at (or the certification it still lacks), which is the actionable half |
| `verified` | **rung 4 or deeper** — enumerable AND read by a gate AND pinned by a retained counter-example — plus an owning document that is governed, claims a verified state, and carries a body-certifying stamp that still covers it |

**Across all nodes:** `sketched` 5 (4%) · `documented` 134 (94%) · `verified` 3 (2%)

`verified` is **3**: those nodes reach rung 4 or deeper and their
owning document carries a body-certifying stamp that still covers it.

**It is also unreachable for most of the map today (`OG-207`):** `verified` requires rung 4 or
deeper, rung 3 means *a registered gate reads this module*, and only **47 of 142**
nodes are at rung 4 or deeper — so 95 cannot reach the top state by any amount
of documentation work.
3 container(s) have no rung-4 module at all (`draft`, `census`, `tests`), so those packages can never report themselves
`verified` whatever their documents say.

## The ratchet

Each container declares a `depthFloor` in `system.spec.json` — a commitment that it will not
get shallower. It is checked in **both** directions: measuring below the floor is a
regression, a floor written beneath the measurement is slack, and a floor written below the
one committed at `HEAD` is a **loosening** — refused whatever today's measurement says,
because lowering the measurement and the floor together used to make both look level.

**What it does NOT constrain (`OG-206`):** depth is the `min` over a container's modules, so
shedding modules can only raise it. A container can lose everything but its shallowest module
and still report level. **Nothing guards the deletion direction** — `blueprint verify` covers
modules ADDED and unclaimed, not modules removed — and ratcheting the module count would fire
on ordinary deletion, which this project has done deliberately before (`OG-73`).

Ratchet memory: **git history of the spec (10 container(s) remembered)**.

| container | floor | measured | state of the shallowest module |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docgen` | 2 | 2 `modules` | `tools.docgen` |
| `moat` | 5 | 5 `detail` | `tools.docgen.hooks` |
| `corpus-check` | 1 | 1 `shape` | `tools.corpus_check.__main__` |
| `health` | 1 | 1 `shape` | `tools.health.__main__` |
| `blueprint` | 1 | 1 `shape` | `tools.blueprint.__main__` |
| `draft` | 1 | 1 `shape` | `tools.draft.__main__` |
| `census` | 1 | 1 `shape` | `tools.census.__main__` |
| `project-index` | 2 | 2 `modules` | `tools.project_index` |
| `lib` | 2 | 2 `modules` | `tools` |
| `tests` | 2 | 2 `modules` | `tools.tests` |

The ratchet is level: every container declares a floor and measures exactly at it.

> **5 container(s) sit at `shape` because their `__main__.py` is a
> delegation shim** (`corpus-check`, `health`, `blueprint`, `draft`, `census`), which has nothing public by design. Rung 2 asks whether a
> module's contents are enumerable and tests it by counting public top-level definitions,
> which a shim legitimately has none of. **Phase 7 decided (`OG-204`) to KEEP this reading:**
> a shim's `sketched` state carries the accurate `why` — *lacks enumerable* — so a reader
> sees exactly what is absent (a public surface), and widening rung 2 to admit any non-empty
> body would move `sketched` to 0 and force four floor-raises in the phase that benefits from
> the change — the self-serving measurement edit `OG-198`/`OG-204` exist to refuse. The
> evidence stays a public surface; the decision, not the metric, is the deliverable.

## The document lifecycle

Six steps, each read from the artifact that owns it. **Nothing here is enforced by this
report** — `classification` gates the tag, `manifest_drift` the wire, `identity` and `stamps`
the version and the stamp. This says how far each governed document has got.

| document | `tag` | `wire` | `date` | `version` | `changelog` | `stamp` | done |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/process/THREAT_MODEL.md` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | ✅ | 5/6 |
| `examples/capability-gallery.md` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | — | 4/6 |
| `tools/docgen/gallery.md` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | — | 4/6 |
| `tools/docgen/sample-multi-figure.md` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | — | 4/6 |
| `tools/docgen/sample.md` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | — | 4/6 |

Only governed documents appear: the lifecycle is a contract a document opts into by carrying
a doc-system header. The count of governed documents is the charter's purpose-2 measurement.
